"""
Project Title: Federated Averaging for CIFAR-10 Classification with Keras (ai-ml-ds-FedAvgCIFAR2025)
File Name: federated_averaging_cifar10.py

Short Description:
Simulates Federated Learning with Keras: CIFAR‑10 is partitioned among multiple clients, each trains a local CNN,
then a central server aggregates via FedAvg. Supports non‑IID splits, multiple rounds, and evaluation of global model.
"""

import numpy as np  # type: ignore
import tensorflow as tf  # type: ignore
from tensorflow.keras import layers, Model, Input  # type: ignore
from tensorflow.keras.datasets import cifar10  # type: ignore

# ----------------------------
# 1. Hyperparameters & Setup
# ----------------------------
NUM_CLIENTS: int = 5             # type: int = number of federated clients
ROUNDS: int = 20                 # type: int = federated training rounds
LOCAL_EPOCHS: int = 2            # type: int = epochs per client
BATCH_SIZE: int = 64             # type: int = batch size
LR: float = 1e-3                 # type: float = learning rate
INPUT_SHAPE: tuple = (32,32,3)    # type: tuple = CIFAR-10 image shape
NUM_CLASSES: int = 10            # type: int = number of classes

# ----------------------------
# 2. Load & Partition CIFAR-10
# ----------------------------
(x_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray), (x_test: np.ndarray, y_test: np.ndarray) = cifar10.load_data()
x_train = x_train.astype("float32")/255.0
x_test  = x_test.astype("float32")/255.0
y_train = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y_train, NUM_CLASSES)
y_test  = tf.keras.utils.to_categorical(y_test, NUM_CLASSES)

# Non-IID partition: each client gets 2 classes
client_data: list = []
labels = np.argmax(y_train, axis=1)
for i in range(NUM_CLIENTS):
    cls = [2*i, 2*i+1]  # each client two classes
    idx = np.where(np.isin(labels, cls))[0]
    np.random.shuffle(idx)
    x_c = x_train[idx]; y_c = y_train[idx]
    client_data.append((x_c, y_c))

# ----------------------------
# 3. Model Builder
# ----------------------------
def build_cnn() -> Model:
    inp: Input = Input(shape=INPUT_SHAPE, name="img")
    x: tf.Tensor = layers.Conv2D(32,3,activation="relu",padding="same")(inp)
    x = layers.MaxPool2D()(x)
    x = layers.Conv2D(64,3,activation="relu",padding="same")(x)
    x = layers.MaxPool2D()(x)
    x = layers.Flatten()(x)
    x = layers.Dense(128, activation="relu")(x)
    out: tf.Tensor = layers.Dense(NUM_CLASSES, activation="softmax")(x)
    model: Model = Model(inp, out)
    model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(LR),
                  loss="categorical_crossentropy",
                  metrics=["accuracy"])
    return model

# Initialize global model
global_model: Model = build_cnn()

# ----------------------------
# 4. Federated Training
# ----------------------------
for rnd in range(1, ROUNDS+1):
    print(f"\n--- Round {rnd} ---")
    # collect client weights
    weights_list: list = []
    for client_idx, (x_c, y_c) in enumerate(client_data):
        local_model: Model = build_cnn()
        local_model.set_weights(global_model.get_weights())
        local_model.fit(x_c, y_c,
                        epochs=LOCAL_EPOCHS,
                        batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
                        verbose=0)
        weights_list.append(local_model.get_weights())
        print(f" Client {client_idx} trained on {x_c.shape[0]} samples")
    # FedAvg: average weights
    new_weights = []
    for layer_weights in zip(*weights_list):
        new_weights.append(
            np.mean(np.stack(layer_weights, axis=0), axis=0)
        )
    global_model.set_weights(new_weights)
    # Evaluate global model on held-out test
    loss, acc = global_model.evaluate(x_test, y_test, batch_size=256, verbose=0)
    print(f" Global model test accuracy: {acc:.4f}")

# ----------------------------
# 5. Example Inference Use Cases
# ----------------------------
# Use Case 1: single image prediction
img0: np.ndarray = x_test[0:1]  # type: np.ndarray
pred0: np.ndarray = global_model.predict(img0)  # type: np.ndarray
print("Example 1 - True label:", np.argmax(y_test[0]), "Predicted:", np.argmax(pred0))

# Use Case 2: batch prediction
imgs: np.ndarray = x_test[100:110]  # type: np.ndarray
preds: np.ndarray = global_model.predict(imgs)
print("Example 2 - Predicted labels batch:", np.argmax(preds, axis=1))

Key Learnings & Research Areas:

  • Federated Averaging (FedAvg): client‑server weight aggregation.
  • Non‑IID Data Simulation: partition by class to mimic realistic heterogeneity.
  • Keras Model Cloning: local training and global weight updates.
  • Use Cases: on‑device learning, privacy‑preserving ML, cross‑device collaboration.

This simulation pushes Keras beyond centralized training into federated paradigms—essential for modern privacy‑aware applications. Continuous extensions: secure aggregation, differential privacy, personalization layers.🚀🔥
